page_title: Crisp: Free BetterDisplay & Lunar alternative for macOS

summary.name: Crisp
summary.one_liner: Crisp is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app for external monitor control, covering HiDPI scaling, DDC hardware brightness, presets, arrangement, and a command line tool.
use_cases: Fix blurry text on an external monitor
Control external monitor brightness from the Mac
Save and apply display setups with presets
Schedule day and night display settings
Switch a monitor between Mac and another computer
Create virtual screens for streaming or headless Macs
summary.what_it_does: Crisp is a menu bar panel for macOS that controls external monitors. It provides HiDPI scaled resolutions and finer-grained scaling on external displays, and brightness control via hardware DDC with a software fallback, including brightness keys. It can unlock HDR brightness reserve on XDR and HDR displays to go past 100%, and adjust monitor speaker volume over DDC. Presets save resolution, brightness, arrangement, image adjustment, HDR, and active displays, and can be applied by click, global shortcut, or Shortcuts automation. A command line tool, crispctl, ships inside the app for scripting these controls.
notable: Open source under MIT license, listed in awesome-mac
Command line tool crispctl and Apple Shortcuts actions
Extra Brightness unlocks HDR brightness reserve on XDR and HDR displays
Virtual HiDPI displays for streaming, sidecar, or headless Macs
caveats: Disconnecting displays from the menu is Apple Silicon only
Support is optional; code signing and notarization costs a $99/year Apple Developer membership
